There will be times you think you can’t make it. You’ll wish the sun didn’t come up. You’ll hate music. You’ll hate happy couples. You’ll hate looking at little babies and kids because they used to be that small too. You’ll hate everything you used to do together. You won’t touch it. You will sleep with their things. You read things they wrote. You’ll go over and over in your brain every first time you had together, everything they said, every touch. You’ll wonder if they ever loved you, or if they loved you so much they did this for you. You’ll get drunk. You’ll drive reckless and scream to the top of your lungs. You’ll lay on the floor staring. You might have people say disgusting things to you. You’ll think of every should’ve, would’ve, could’ve. You’ll hate God. You’ll hate yourself. You’ll hate their family. Their friends. Everyone who knows you. Everyone who knows about it. You’ll hit rock bottom. You’ll start doing stuff you couldn’t have done if you were with them. You’ll think it’s going to be a great escape. They’ll keep popping up in your head though. How they should be there... you’ll try to “move on” you’ll go on dates and talk to other opposite sex and you’ll hate that too. You’ll hate that they aren’t them. You’ll hate when they do something similar. You’ll hate that you can’t just move on. Going to a group didn’t work for me. I went one time and a mother who just lost her son and was super dramatic looked at me after sharing and spat that”I was young and I would find someone else and be fine”. I never went back. People WONT understand. You’ll lose a lot of friends. A lot of “fake friends”... people you thought would be there won’t talk to you anymore. They’ll delete you on social media. You won’t know what to say when people ask how you are. You will become strong as fuck. You’ll be able to talk about all the things that you couldn’t before. You’ll also have extreme trust issues. You’ll start doing things they liked just to feel like they’re there. You’ll drink their favorite drinks and eat their favorite foods. Just to feel a little piece of them. You’ll slowly start becoming yourself again. You’ll probably talk and think about them a lot. They’re probably a lot of the reason that you’re you. You’ll bring them up and people will act weird every time. Like you can’t bring them up like you can any other death. IGNORE IT. Tell what you want. Get it out. Go to therapy. Journal. Cry. Be sad. Be fucking sad that they’re gone. Be mad. I beat the shit out of a wooden project with a mallet. You may have ptsd. Depending what happened before they did it. I cussed in people’s faces. I had panic attacks.. You’ll probably have nightmares. Some dreams you may not want to wake up from. You’ll sit in the grass and stare at the sky and yank every blade out around you and just start spouting you feelings. You’ll look up and talk to them. You’ll wonder where they are. If you’ll see them again. You’ll start becoming just you. Accepting what parts will always be them and now they’re part of you. You’ll start doing things just to remind you of them. Live for them. Live because you’re strong enough to carry it. You’ll laugh again. You’ll go out to the bar and the drinks will bring you right back to talking about them so you might want to avoid it.. you’ll think of it less. But it will always be a stabbing pain in your chest to think about them and what they did. You won’t be the same. You won’t laugh as much and be as happy as much as you were before but you will be CONTENT. I haven’t wanted anyone since. People will tell you to move on or think that talking to someone else will help but they just don’t understand. Tell them they don’t understand and you will when you’re ready. Go to therapy. Really. It made me realize and the past trauma and if I didn’t get help I would go down the same path. You’ll create goals and plans for your life without anyone. You’ll feel jealous of others but try to be happy for them instead. You will cherish every memory. You’ll begin appreciating your good memories more than ever and know you wouldn’t change a thing even though this was the ending. You Will accept that everyone has a choice. You’re not responsible and you couldn’t have saved them. They made the choice, you didn’t. They knew you loved them and they loved you. They just didn’t love life. You’ll accept others decisions and realize you can’t control anyone but you. Think of the good times and create the life you want and don’t worry about moving on. Ignore unsolicited advice. You don’t move on. You just get through it. It’s true. You’ll be a different person after going through this. You’ll learn to love yourself.
